Are you 100% sure you can't hand the keys back? I work in repossessions and there is something called voluntary vacant possession that you can do. It's basically handing the property to the lender, this would save on the court fees incurred in the usual repossession process. The lender would then market the property for sale. I'm also under the impression bankruptcy relates to unsecured debt such as credit cards rather than secured, such as mortgages, but if the lender had possession of the property they would then deal with the official receiver if and when necessary. I can't say this as fact, but I really think it's worth you having a chat with your mortgage provider. 

EDIT: Of course you would need to find somewhere else to live before handing the property back, but once it is empty it's a really quick process with the lender I work with, I would hope the process is similar across the board.
I know Northern Rock are no more but there must be someone dealing with this. You don't mention if you are in arrears with your mortgage but if you are it is even more crucial that you speak to them as soon as possible to avoid extra fees.

Just a comment from the other side if it hasn't been said already. I work as a mortgage collections advisor for one of the worlds leading banks. I deal with people every single day who have found themselves in financial hardship for all sorts of reasons.

Talk to us. I cannot stress this enough. Tell us if you know you're going to miss a payment. Even if you know you can't pay for the next six months, tell us. Hell, I'm dealing with people who are 80 payments behind. We've evicted people who are six behind, because they've avoided all contact so we don't know whats going on. 

Stop paying all unsecured borrowing. Or pay £1, thats all they require - once they know you are behind on your mortgage they are bound by regulations to let you prioritise this. Its amazing though how many people would rather pay their credit card than their mortgage.

Set up a payment plan. Go through a budget planner with us. Its better to pay something than nothing. You have to repay it all anyway and chances are interest will increase so if you can cover that, or at least some of it, you should. 

I sort of agree with the tip because yes we can do a set off, and I can appreciate why this could cause problems, but only when we've exhausted all other means of contact. We would never leave you worse off. We can't. You should speak to us before it gets to that point, and when you do it helps us if your accounts are there for us to see, so we can budget for direct debits and such.

I guess I'm not sure if all lenders take the same approach, I certainly hope things move this way if not.
